title: Study Skills
summary: Learning styles, time management and study timetables, effective study methods (summaries, mind maps, mnemonics), preparing for exams and managing exam stress.

rows: Reading aloud, discussing, recording and listening to notes
Models, experiments, flash cards, walking while revising

notes.text: Most people use a **mix** of styles. Using several methods helps you remember more.

items: Make a **study timetable** that includes school, homework, study, chores, sport, rest and sleep.
Study in **short sessions** (about 30 to 45 minutes) with 5 to 10 minute breaks.
Do the hardest subject when you are most alert.
Avoid **procrastination** (putting things off): start with a small task to get going.
Remove distractions: put your phone away or on silent.

notes.title: Planning an afternoon
notes.problem: You have 3 hours after school and must study maths and history, do chores and rest. Plan it.
steps: Do the hardest work first when you are freshest.
Maths 1 hour, break 15 minutes, history 45 minutes, chores 30 minutes, then rest.
notes.answer: Hard work first, with breaks in between.

rows: Write key points in your own words, using headings and bullet points
Put the main topic in the centre and branch out with key ideas, keywords, colours and pictures
Memory aids such as acronyms (e.g. MAIN for the causes of World War I) or rhymes
Question or term on one side, answer on the other; test yourself
Practise under exam conditions and check with the memo
Explaining a topic to a friend shows whether you really understand it

notes.label: The SQ3R method
notes.text: **S**urvey (skim headings and pictures), **Q**uestion (turn headings into questions), **R**ead (read carefully to answer them), **R**ecite (say or write the answers without looking), **R**eview (go over the work regularly).

notes.title: Passive or active?
notes.problem: Which works better: re-reading your notes, or closing the book and writing down what you remember?
steps: Re-reading can feel easy without being effective.
Recalling information strengthens memory and shows what you don't know.

items: Start revising **weeks** before the exam, not the night before.
Sleep well (8 to 10 hours), eat healthily and drink water.
Pack your equipment the night before.
In the exam: read the instructions and all the questions first; plan your time according to the marks; answer easy questions first; check your work at the end.
Look at **action verbs**: *name/list* (short facts), *describe* (give details), *explain* (give reasons: why/how), *discuss* (give different sides), *compare* (similarities and differences).
A little stress helps you focus; too much makes it hard to think.
Use deep breathing: breathe in for four counts, hold for four, out for four.
Talk to someone if you feel overwhelmed. SADAG offers free support (0800 567 567).
